Argus got the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop at 22:55 UTC and brought in the Investigator Agent. The agent looked at metrics, recent production changes and logs, and placed the start at 22:48. It traced the errors to the monthly-spend-feature flag, which was switched on at that time. The flag turned on a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, so account page requests failed and the error rate went from about 1% to about 32%. No deploy or config change was involved.

At 22:56 Argus switched monthly-spend-feature from ON to OFF. By 22:58 the service had been back to normal since 22:57, the alert had stopped firing, and the incident was marked MITIGATED. The flag is still off.

Argus also opened a draft pull request with a fix for someone to review and merge: https://github.invalid/ohadraz/repository/pull/1. It also wrote a postmortem: the outage lasted 9 minutes, 27.4% of requests failed (35.5% at the worst point), and revenue came in about 5,410.09 USD below the same hours in earlier weeks.

Turning the flag off didn't remove the bug. The division in the monthly spend code is still there, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on before the fix is merged would likely break account pages again for shoppers who haven't bought anything this month.
